public.title: Assert Lite
public.description: input is an array of assertions {op,actual,expected}; op is equal or truthy. Equal compares JSON structure ignoring object key order. Truthy uses JavaScript truthiness and ignores expected. Return one boolean per assertion. This adapter returns assertion outcomes rather than throwing. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.

explanation: Recursively compare own keys and values, preserving array order; dispatch truthiness separately. Time and stack are linear in the total value size and nesting depth. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
